gui_sequences.per_step: action, expected, outcome on screen (checked before capture), Infra MCP state and version, every MCP call with arguments and result, virtual time, matching acceptance check
gui_sequences.reproducibility: two consecutive runs gave byte-identical screenshots, sequences.json and run.json; Chromium runs with --disable-gpu --num-raster-threads=1 --disable-partial-raster and the page request IDs come from a counter in session storage (GUI source unchanged); another machine or Chromium build can differ by a few anti-aliased pixels

trace.page_requests: writes and previews listed with raw arguments and raw reply (HTTP status and JSON body), unshortened, including tokens and fee breakdowns
trace.ownership: every call (page reads and tool discovery, page writes and previews, forced calls, second Agent reads and writes, Infra events, clock moves, the seed load, inspector snapshot reads) is owned when it is sent by the step open at that moment; the page load before the first sequence is owned by the setup (not listed in run.json); the two pieces of work between sequences have owners of their own and are the two entries of run.json between_sequences; a reply never changes ownership
trace.freeze: read the version, run the check, wait until nothing the step owns is outstanding, read the App's state; a version change since before the check stops the script; observations, version, virtual time and calls come from the frozen state; the wait and scrolling before the screenshot come after the freeze
trace.terminal_outcome: exactly one per call: the reply, or a failure with HTTP status and error
trace.forced_calls: identified by a header token bound to the exact tool and arguments it was issued for; a token sent with any other call stops the script
trace.errors: append-only, including a failed close of the second Agent client: a stop that a caller catches is still reported by later checks and by the teardown check; the client handle is kept until its process has exited, so the close can be retried
stops_on: a call sent with no owner, including after the last sequence until the browser closes
a version change between a step's check and its freeze
a call sent after its step was frozen
a failed call or a second terminal outcome
a forced-call token sent with another call
a submitting step without a write or forced call

app_load_digest.algorithm: SHA-256 over each file's package-relative path, a NUL byte and its bytes, in path order (the verifier's digestTree applied to the included files)
app_load_digest.note: The verifier digest of the whole package (app.package_sha256) cannot be recorded inside the package; the commit is named in the submission comment.

browser.macos_date_field: on macOS Chromium draws the native date field in the operating system regional format whatever the locale; values are checked in ISO form

delivery_dataset.design: base seed (dataset/base.json, 2025-01-01T00:00:00-05:00, account and catalog, no orders) plus dated replay (dataset/replay.json, 1518 steps: 913 account-holder tool calls, 605 Infra events) through the App handlers; dataset/full.json is the end state
delivery_dataset.as_of: dataset/as-of.cjs --at <instant> replays only the steps before the instant through the handlers and commits the timers due before it (timers_committed); each selection has its own seed ID (instant to the millisecond and a content hash); its bundle cites only the delivery-dataset source; later Infra events on selected objects are returned for staging, and orders still open are listed with their withheld account-holder steps
delivery_dataset.fixture_relation: fixtures/minimal.json is unchanged; it and the dataset share the account and catalog (equal at the fixture clock, tests/t26-dataset.test.cjs) with independent order histories

gaps.reason: DoorDash is only the workflow reference. The approved proposal (proposals/environment/plateway-delivery.md, line 96: "N/A: no crawling or copied menus") excludes collecting its data, and Plateway's restaurants, menus, couriers and account are invented, so there is no real source to collect around November 2026; the whole window is synthetic.
The 613 notices are in the App's own notice log only; the dataset holds no Mail history for them. Mail is optional, and the Mail sender treats notices present in a loaded seed as history.

distinct_dates.basis: Counted over the records loaded into the App (dataset/full.json), which Agents and Infra read back.
distinct_dates.note: The global count over both sources adds 21 days on which the replay log holds only 26 cart edits and 27 menu or restaurant events; those days have no App record.
